current_p1_ru: Симпсоны, Бивис и Баттхед, Женаты с детьми, Альф. Ты любишь сериалы, которые смеются над реальностью. Не «развлекают»; а критикуют.
current_p1_en:
The Simpsons, Beavis and Butt-Head, Married... with Children, ALF. You love series that laugh at reality. Not "entertain"; criticize.
This works because you have critical thinking. Just laughing isn't enough; the laughter has to be smart.
People sometimes don't share it: "Beavis is dumb". Dumb? It was one of the sharpest satires on American youth.
What's worth knowing: '90s satire often seems "insufficiently politically correct" today. Learn to read cultural context. What was funny in 1995 may have aged; what was accurate stayed accurate.

current_p1_ru: Беверли-Хиллз 90210, Мелроуз-Плейс, Баффи, Друзья. Тебе нравились подростковые драмы 90-х. Школа, любовь, дружба, кризисы — всё, что определило твоё поколение.
current_p1_en:
Beverly Hills 90210, Melrose Place, Buffy, Friends. You loved '90s teen dramas. School, love, friendship, crises — everything that defined your generation.
Why it works: you have memory of teenage life. These series aren't "fantasy"; this is your life packaged into episodes.
People are sometimes surprised: "you still watch?". Sometimes. And it's a different experience — watching as an adult what you loved as a teenager.
What's worth knowing: '90s teen series often romanticize reality. Learn to tell the difference. Real school was closer to pain than to 90210. That's normal — fiction makes things prettier.

current_p1_ru: Санта-Барбара, Дикий ангел, Тропиканка, Мелроуз-Плейс. Ты вырос(-ла) на «мыльных операх». Бесконечные сюжеты, страсти, любовь, ненависть, измены.
current_p1_en:
Santa Barbara, Wild Angel, Tropikanka, Melrose Place. You grew up on "soap operas". Endless plots, passions, love, hate, betrayals.
It works because you love big drama. Restrained European series bore you; you need it bright.
People sometimes get snobby: "Santa Barbara, really…". Really. It's an era. And I'm at home in it.
What's worth knowing: Latin series often run for years and lose quality. If you got stuck in one — that's normal. Not every series has to be "finished"; some stay with you just as background.

current_p1_ru: Улицы разбитых фонарей, Агент национальной безопасности, Санта-Барбара, Дикий ангел. Ты вырос(-ла) на 90-х в России. Менты, бандиты, бандитский Питер — это была фоновая картинка детства.
current_p1_en:
Streets of Broken Lights, Agent of National Security, Santa Barbara, Wild Angel. You grew up on the Russian '90s. Cops, gangsters, gangster Petersburg — that was the background of childhood.
The reason it works: you have cultural memory. These series aren't "entertainment" — they're a document of an era.
People sometimes don't understand: "those cop shows?". Those cop shows. They tell more about Russia in the '90s than a textbook.
What's worth knowing: the '90s now get romanticized (or demonized). Learn to watch these series as ethnographic document. They show a reality that's gone, and the further away it gets, the more valuable they are.

current_p1_ru: Скорая помощь, Твин Пикс, Секретные материалы, Баффи. Ты любил(-а) серьёзные драмы. Не комедии и не подростковые шоу; а сериалы с настоящими ставками.
current_p1_en:
ER, Twin Peaks, The X-Files, Buffy. You loved serious dramas. Not comedies and not teen shows; series with real stakes.
This works because you have a grown-up relationship with TV. Just being entertained isn't enough; the show has to be art.
People are sometimes surprised: "ER, really?". Of course. It was the best medical drama of its time.
What's worth knowing: ER of the '90s is the benchmark for medical drama. Modern shows (House, Grey's Anatomy) are its descendants. Learn to watch the classics. Without them, modern shows make less sense.

current_p1_ru: Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, Chaumet, Piaget. Ты в мире французского ювелирного искусства. Это не «украшения», это история — короли, императоры, парижские ателье.
current_p1_en:
Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, Chaumet, Piaget. You're in the world of French jewelry. These aren't "accessories", they're history — kings, emperors, Parisian ateliers.
It works because you have a feel for heritage. You understand: a jewel isn't an accessory, it's an artifact.
People sometimes don't tell them apart: "Cartier is just Cartier". You know each house has its own signature, legends, collections.
What's worth knowing: the French school is the peak, but also peak prices. Learn to value more accessible but quality alternatives too. Not every piece needs to be from a French house to be beautiful.

current_p1_ru: Bvlgari, Buccellati, Pomellato, Damiani. Ты в итальянской традиции — там, где украшения выразительны, объёмны, с характером. Не «тонкая нота»; полная мощь.
current_p1_en:
Bvlgari, Buccellati, Pomellato, Damiani. You're in the Italian tradition — where jewelry is expressive, voluminous, with character. Not a "subtle note"; full force.
The reason it works: you love expression. French subtlety bores you; you need passion.
People are sometimes surprised: "that's a lot". A lot — and beautiful. Different things.
What's worth knowing: the Italian school is strong but sometimes goes overboard. Learn to feel the line. A bold piece is beautiful, but in the wrong context, it shouts.

current_p1_ru: Graff, Harry Winston, De Beers, Cartier. Ты ценишь камни. Не просто украшение — а конкретный бриллиант или сапфир, с историей, с весом, с легендой.
current_p1_en:
Graff, Harry Winston, De Beers, Cartier. You value the stones. Not just the piece — a specific diamond or sapphire, with history, weight, legend.
This works because you have a relationship with the material. What matters is not just "how it was made" but "what from".
People are sometimes surprised: "Graff is only for millionaires". In commercial terms — yes. In understanding — for everyone. Knowing what a real stone is — that's an education, not a purchase.
What's worth knowing: real big stones are an investment, and not everyone can afford them. Learn to value craft of the cut and rarity, not just size. Carat matters, but a perfectly cut smaller stone can be more beautiful than a clumsy big one.

current_p1_ru: Mikimoto, Tasaki, Buccellati, Piaget. Ты любишь, когда в украшении есть тонкость и жесткость одновременно. Японский жемчуг с азиатской смелостью, итальянская резьба с японской точностью.
current_p1_en:
Mikimoto, Tasaki, Buccellati, Piaget. You love when a piece holds subtlety and toughness at once. Japanese pearls with Asian boldness, Italian carving with Japanese precision.
Why it works: you have a non-standard view. Classical European tradition bores you; you need something with a different temperament.
People sometimes don't get it: "Mikimoto is just pearls". Not just pearls — the start of an entire cultured-pearl industry. It's history.
What's worth knowing: Eastern houses are less represented abroad. Learn to look. And remember — Mikimoto and Tasaki are best seen in their flagship boutiques, not in tourist outlets.

current_p1_ru: Tiffany, Harry Winston, Graff, Chopard. Эти дома одевают звёзд на красную дорожку. Ты любишь украшения, у которых есть медийный шарм.
current_p1_en:
Tiffany, Harry Winston, Graff, Chopard. These houses dress stars for the red carpet. You love jewelry with media charm.
It works because you love glam. You're not embarrassed — you understand that beauty on stage and in film shapes culture.
People sometimes get snobby: "Tiffany is for teens". It's for everyone. And their "blue box" became a cultural phenomenon for a reason.
What's worth knowing: Hollywood glam goes mass quickly. Today's Tiffany & Co. isn't the same brand as 30 years ago. Learn to tell classic collections from commercial spinoffs.

current_p1_ru: Chow Tai Fook, Mikimoto, Tasaki, Bvlgari. Тебе ближе восточный взгляд. Гонконгское золото, японский жемчуг, итальянский орнамент — всё это говорит о наследии, о традиции, о ремесле, передаваемом через поколения.
current_p1_en:
Chow Tai Fook, Mikimoto, Tasaki, Bvlgari. You're closer to the Eastern view. Hong Kong gold, Japanese pearls, Italian ornament — all of it speaks of heritage, tradition, craft passed through generations.
The reason it works: you love roots. Modern Western brands feel "soulless" to you; Eastern ones keep ties to lineage.
People are sometimes surprised: "Chow Tai Fook? that's Chinese". Chinese. And one of the most respected jewelry houses in the world.
What's worth knowing: Eastern houses often work in traditional aesthetics that can seem "not modern". That's not a flaw — it's a choice. Learn to see beauty outside the European framework.

current_p1_ru: Pomellato, Chopard, Damiani, Van Cleef. Ты любишь дома, которые умеют делать традиционное в современном звучании. Не «классика для бабушек», а актуальные коллекции, в которых есть и история, и сегодня.
current_p1_en:
Pomellato, Chopard, Damiani, Van Cleef. You love houses that do the traditional in a modern voice. Not "classics for grandmothers" but current collections that hold both history and today.
This works because you understand: luxury shouldn't be outdated. Houses that don't update lose the young buyer — and with them the future.
People sometimes say: "you have classical taste". Not classical — modern. Different things.
What's worth knowing: modern collections sometimes lose the magic of the classics. Look at both. The best houses keep the dialogue between tradition and now.

current_p1_ru: Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Ferrari, Mercedes. Это бренды, которые продают не товар — а статус и эстетику. И ты понимаешь это. Тебе важно не только то, что вещь делает, но и что она говорит о тебе.
current_p1_en:
Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Ferrari, Mercedes. These are brands that sell not the product — but status and aesthetics. And you understand it. What matters isn't only what the thing does, but what it says about you.
It works because you have a mature relationship with brands. You don't "buy Chanel to flex"; you value the design, the tradition, the quality, and status comes as a bonus.
People sometimes don't get it: "why Ferrari in Moscow?". Because Ferrari isn't a car — it's an engineering marvel.
What's worth knowing: luxury works if it's in your context. A Chanel bag in a student dorm can look out of place, no matter the price. Learn to read the context.

current_p1_ru: Mercedes, BMW, Lufthansa, Apple. Тебя цепляет инженерная мощь. Не «дороговизна» сама по себе; а уверенность, что вещь сделана с понятием, что внутри — реальная сложность.
current_p1_en:
Mercedes, BMW, Lufthansa, Apple. What draws you in is engineering power. Not "expensive" by itself; the certainty that the thing was made with understanding, that there's real complexity inside.
The reason it works: you have respect for craft. Most people see only the surface; you understand under the hood is years of development.
People sometimes don't tell them apart: "Mercedes is Mercedes". You know — there's the S-class, and there are budget Mercedes, and they're different worlds.
What's worth knowing: engineering power has a price. Maintaining a BMW is more expensive than buying it. Learn to look at total cost of ownership, not just purchase price. The most beautiful machine becomes a burden if you can't sustain it.

current_p1_ru: Apple, Google, Amazon. Это компании, которые формируют наше будущее. Ты не просто пользуешься их продуктами — ты понимаешь, что они меняют мир.
current_p1_en:
Apple, Google, Amazon. These are companies shaping our future. You don't just use their products — you understand they're changing the world.
This works because you have macro vision. Most people see a phone; you see ecosystem, policy, cultural influence.
People sometimes say: "you really admire them". Not "admire" — analyze. Their influence is too big to ignore.
What's worth knowing: tech giants are also a concentration risk. The more of you in their ecosystem, the more dependence. Learn to keep freedom — backups, alternative services, the ability to leave. Otherwise you're a hostage to their decisions.

current_p1_ru: Nike, Red Bull, Ferrari, BMW. Это бренды энергии. Не для медленной жизни; для движения, для победы, для всё-сейчас.
current_p1_en:
Nike, Red Bull, Ferrari, BMW. These are energy brands. Not for the slow life; for motion, for victory, for everything-now.
Why it works: you have an internal drive. You need things that match your tempo.
People are sometimes surprised: "you're not a pro athlete". Not pro. But I live like I am.
What's worth knowing: "sporty" brands sometimes become a style without the actual training behind it. If you're all in Nike with no gym days, that's marketing self-deception. Learn to tell.

current_p1_ru: McDonald's, Starbucks, Coca-Cola, Red Bull. Это бренды повседневности — то, что в каждой стране, в каждом аэропорту, в каждом плохом моменте, когда нужно немного знакомого.
current_p1_en:
McDonald's, Starbucks, Coca-Cola, Red Bull. These are brands of the everyday — what's in every country, every airport, every bad moment when you need a little familiar.
It works because you have no snobbery. You understand Starbucks isn't "the best coffee", but it's standardized everywhere, and that's its strength.
People sometimes accuse: "you know it's bad for you". I know. And sometimes I still need it.
What's worth knowing: mass brands are also a culture and a health system. If you're at McDonald's every day, that's not "convenience", it's a habit. Learn to use these brands as occasional pleasure, not the default.

current_p1_ru: Disney, Coca-Cola, McDonald's, Starbucks. Эти бренды связаны с воспоминаниями. Ты не «фанат», ты помнишь — мама приводила в McDonald's, ёлка с Coca-Cola, кино Disney в детстве.
current_p1_en:
Disney, Coca-Cola, McDonald's, Starbucks. These brands tie to memories. You're not a "fan" — you remember: mom took you to McDonald's, the Coca-Cola Christmas tree, Disney films in childhood.
The reason it works: you have cultural memory. You understand these brands aren't just business; they're shared fabric of an entire generation's childhood.
People sometimes get snobby: "Disney is for kids". For kids. And those kids live in us.
What's worth knowing: nostalgia for these brands is normal. But don't confuse real memories with marketing triggers. Disney professionally sells nostalgia, and sometimes you pay for the feeling, not for what's actually there.

current_p1_ru: Playboy, Disney, Louis Vuitton, Chanel. Это не просто бренды — это целые культурные институции. Их логотипы появляются в фильмах, в живописи, в музыке. Они часть истории.
current_p1_en:
Playboy, Disney, Louis Vuitton, Chanel. These aren't just brands — they're cultural institutions. Their logos appear in films, paintings, music. They're part of history.
This works because you understand the scale. Most people see a logo; you see a century of culture.
People sometimes don't share it: "Playboy is sexism". It was. Now it's also cultural archeology and a feminist subject. The brand evolves, and its history is complicated.
What's worth knowing: cultural brands live long, but not forever. Today's legends can be tomorrow's outdated. Watch which of them keep relevance and which become museum pieces.

current_p1_ru: Турция, Египет, Таиланд, Шри-Ланка. Ты выбираешь пляжный отдых не «премиум», а нормальный — где море, песок, тепло, и не разоряет.
current_p1_en:
Turkey, Egypt, Thailand, Sri Lanka. You pick beach vacation not as "premium" but as normal — where there's sea, sand, warmth, and it doesn't break the bank.
It works because you know what rest is for. You don't need to pay for status; you need to actually relax.
People sometimes get snobby: "Turkey is basic." Basic. And I'm comfortable there.
What's worth knowing: mass tourism has a price — packed beaches, all-inclusive hotels with monotonous food. Learn to pick locations within a popular country. Turkey has quiet places too, not just Antalya.

current_p1_ru: Мальдивы, Бора-Бора, Сейшелы, ОАЭ. Тебе нужен люкс. Не «вилла на пляже», а «бунгало на воде». Это другое отношение к отдыху и другие деньги.
current_p1_en:
Maldives, Bora-Bora, Seychelles, UAE. You need luxury. Not just "a villa by the beach" — an overwater bungalow. This is a different relationship with rest and different money.
It works because you have both means and understanding of value. These places aren't just "rich-person flexing"; they're a different kind of ocean experience.
People sometimes accuse: "for that money you could go to Turkey three times." You could. But one Maldives trip leaves more memories than three average ones.
What's worth knowing: premium islands require long planning and a serious budget. Plan ahead. And remember — these are places to go for impression, not just to tick off a standard week. Save up and go thoughtfully.

current_p1_ru: Испания, Италия, Греция, Португалия. Ты любишь южную Европу. Не «острова» — а целая культура: еда, история, архитектура плюс море.
current_p1_en:
Spain, Italy, Greece, Portugal. You love southern Europe. Not just islands — a whole culture: food, history, architecture, and the sea.
It works because you want the full package. "Just the beach" bores you; you need to also do museums, restaurants, walking around.
People sometimes don't get it: "why Greece, you can do Turkey." You can do Turkey. You want Greece.
What's worth knowing: Mediterranean rest is more expensive than mass-market. But the impressions are different. Invest in longer trips — 7 days in Greece gives more than 3 days on a tour.

current_p1_ru: Бали, Мексика, Куба, Таиланд. Тебе нужны тропики — настоящие, с пальмами, бунгало и тёплым океаном. Не европейское море; а карибское или индийское.
current_p1_en:
Bali, Mexico, Cuba, Thailand. You need the tropics — real ones, with palms, bungalows, warm ocean. Not European sea; Caribbean or Indian.
Why it lands: you have a passion for the exotic. Europe is already familiar; you need something further.
People sometimes worry: "so a long flight." Far. And every time, worth it.
What's worth knowing: tropics are also a serious time-zone and climate shift. If you fly for 7 days, half goes to recovery. Plan trips of at least 10 days — otherwise you don't fully enjoy.

current_p1_ru: Австралия, Португалия, Индонезия, Шри-Ланка. Ты выбираешь места с большой водой. Не закрытое море; а океан с волнами, со своим характером.
current_p1_en:
Australia, Portugal, Indonesia, Sri Lanka. You pick places with big water. Not enclosed sea; ocean with waves and its own character.
The logic is simple: you love big water. "Lying on the beach" bores you; you need something to do with the water.
People sometimes don't get it: "you're a surfer?." Not pro. But I love the ocean, and these places have the best.
What's worth knowing: "ocean" places often don't have all-inclusive. You organize yourself. Accept it. It's a different rest format — more movement, less pool-lounging.

current_p1_ru: Мексика, Куба, Бора-Бора, Сейшелы. Тебе нужна карибская атмосфера — расслабленность, музыка, цвета. Это не Европа; это другая ментальность.
current_p1_en:
Mexico, Cuba, Bora-Bora, Seychelles. You need the Caribbean atmosphere — relaxedness, music, colors. This isn't Europe; this is a different mentality.
It works because you want a different rhythm. European structured vacations feel too tight; you need "let it be as it is."
People sometimes worry: "there's risk there." Sometimes. And sometimes worth it. Life without risk isn't quite that.
What's worth knowing: Caribbean countries vary in safety and infrastructure. Research the specific place. Cuba and the Maldives are different worlds, both in the tropics.

current_p1_ru: Таиланд, Шри-Ланка, Индонезия, Мальдивы. Ты любишь Восток — другая культура, другая еда, другие традиции, плюс тропический океан.
current_p1_en:
Thailand, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Maldives. You love the East — different culture, food, traditions, plus tropical ocean.
It works because you have cultural curiosity. "Lying around" isn't enough; you need time inside the unfamiliar.
People are sometimes surprised: "Asia again?." Again. And every time it's different.
What's worth knowing: Asian destinations require adaptation. Food, climate, sometimes language — all different. If first time, don't try to "see everything." Better to go deep in one place than skim three.

current_p1_ru: Дьявол носит Prada, Деловая девушка, С девяти до пяти, Доброе утро. Тебя вдохновляют героини, которые работают и не извиняются. Без слёз о том, что «трудно совмещать»; просто строят карьеру и живут.
current_p1_en:
The Devil Wears Prada, Working Girl, Nine to Five, Morning Glory. You're inspired by heroines who work and don't apologize. No speeches about "how hard it is to balance it all"; they build careers and live.
The logic is simple: you have your own attitude toward work. Films where "a woman suffers over choosing family or career" bore you; you want action.
People sometimes call it "not feminist": "well where's the feminism?." And feminism is exactly that: doing things without having to defend your right to do them.
What's worth knowing: career films sometimes miss complexity. Real life often holds more compromise than screen versions admit. Use them as inspiration, not as a checklist. The heroine on screen has a screenwriter on her side; you have only yourself.

current_p1_ru: Эрин Брокович, Скрытые фигуры, Норма Рэй, Силквуд. Тебе нравятся фильмы, основанные на правдивых событиях. Реальные женщины, реальная борьба, реальная победа (или цена за неё).
current_p1_en:
Erin Brockovich, Hidden Figures, Norma Rae, Silkwood. You're drawn to films based on true events. Real women, real fight, real victory (or the price for it).
It works because you have respect for the actual. Fictional stories are wonderful, but sometimes the addition "based on true events" changes the whole perception — you understand it happened.
People sometimes wonder: "so truth hooks you?" Yes. And that's not a bad thing.
What's worth knowing: "based on true events" is usually heavily dramatized. The real Erin Brockovich is not identical to the heroine onscreen. Learn to keep this in mind. Cinematic truth and biographical truth are different genres. Inspiration — yes. Literal copying of the heroine — careful.

current_p1_ru: Прислуга, Скрытые фигуры, Улыбка Моны Лизы, Норма Рэй. Тебя цепляют истории про эпохи, когда женщины и меньшинства боролись за свои базовые права. И ты знаешь — без этих женщин не было бы того мира, в котором мы живём.
current_p1_en:
The Help, Hidden Figures, Mona Lisa Smile, Norma Rae. You're drawn to stories about eras when women and minorities fought for basic rights. And you know — without these women there wouldn't be the world we live in.
It works because you have historical consciousness. You understand today's norm is a victory, and it isn't yet everywhere.
People sometimes say: "that was 50 years ago." Yes. And the consequences live on. And the fight too.
What's worth knowing: historical films inspire, but sometimes become a way to say "everything's fine now, thanks." The real fight continues. Learn to see modern struggle too. Otherwise you live in a museum of victories while the front line is still active.

current_p1_ru: Тельма и Луиза, Безумный Макс: Дорога ярости, Перспективная девушка, Чудо-женщина. Тебе нравятся героини, которые не подчиняются. Они либо ломают систему, либо убегают от неё. И в обоих случаях — побеждают.
current_p1_en:
Thelma & Louise, Mad Max: Fury Road, Promising Young Woman, Wonder Woman. You like heroines who don't submit. They either break the system or run from it. And in both cases — they win, even when the cost is high.
It works because you have a protest nerve. You understand that sometimes "correct behavior" is part of the problem, and you have to break it.
People sometimes worry: "they're romanticizing violence." Not violence — justice. Sometimes, on screen, they overlap.
What's worth knowing: rebellion films are catharsis, not a behavior model. Thelma and Louise don't survive in the finale; Max went through many circles of hell. Learn to take from them the energy, not the road map. The screen forgives mistakes; reality doesn't.
